page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-1xL4 is a KVM-based virtual server configured with 16 vCPUs and 192.0 GB of system memory. The processing power is delivered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz across 16 physical cores with a single thread per core. This instance features a shared CPU allocation model. For hardware acceleration, it bundles a single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression/decompression tests, such as gzip and bzip3. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth is strong at 223.85 GB/sec, while write bandwidth and small-block read bandwidth remain in the average tier. In LLM inference benchmarks using a small 135M model, the system delivers top-tier text generation speeds of 339.34 tokens per second, alongside average prompt processing speeds.

The qualitative cost profile of this server is defined by its high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core and the inclusion of enterprise GPU acceleration, offset by the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage. This resource density makes it suitable for memory-intensive GPU workloads, small-scale LLM inference, and parallel data processing. It is designed for workloads such as machine learning inference, data science pipelines, and memory-heavy analytical tasks that do not require dedicated CPU pinning or local disk storage.
